summary: Tōru Funayama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner, later serving as Associate Professor at Kyushu University (c. 1994–1999) and Professor at Kyoto University (c. 2009–2016).
U Dhammissara specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (c. 2015–2017), studying under Sanu Mahatthanadull and Walmoruwe Piyaratana.
Ugyen Pelgen works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He completed a master's degree at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme from c. 1988 to 1992, and held a post at SOAS University of London around 1994.

Ulrich Timme Kragh specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. After studying at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and University of Copenhagen, he held posts at Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, Sydney, ANU, and the University of Copenhagen.

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who earned her PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg before becoming Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford around 2010.

Uma Chakravarti is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Miranda House (c. 1958–1961) and the University of Delhi (c. 1975–1981) under doctoral supervisor D. Devahuti.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology. He studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam, and held positions at FRLHT, the University of Toyama, and Amala Institute of Medical Sciences.

Unrai Wogihara was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (c. 1909–1926) and Taisho University (c. 1926–1937).
Uranchimeg B. Ujeed works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate at the University of Cambridge from c. 2009 to 2017.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning a PhD at UC Berkeley, she held posts at UC Berkeley, National University of Mongolia, Yonsei University, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis, and the University of Iceland.

Urs App specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Fribourg and Temple University under Richard DeMartino, Yoshitaka Iriya, and Seizan Yanagida, later holding posts at Hanazono University and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Ute Hüsken is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at the University of Göttingen and held a post at Heidelberg University around 2017.
V. A. Gadgil is an Indology scholar who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

V. Raghavan was an Indologist who earned his PhD under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras. He served at the University of Madras from 1935 to 1969 and was secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading (c. 2012–2017) and held a post there around 2017.
Vajragupta works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has served as director of the Birmingham Buddhist Centre (1997) and director of the Triratna Buddhist Community.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University, and held academic posts at Meiji Gakuin University, Princeton University, and the University of Hawaii.

Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her master's thesis at the University of Oslo (c. 2007–2009) under Per Kvaerne and Hanna Havnevik.
Vasily Radlov was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1854–1858) and later held a post at Kunstkamera (c. 1894–1918).
